title: Rank It, Then Ask It: Input Reranking for Maximizing the Performance of LLMs on Symmetric Tasks

problem.claim: When a symmetric task contains many elements, LLMs may overlook some elements and produce inaccurate responses.

gap.claim: LLM inputs are ordered sequences even though symmetric-task inputs are unordered, and certain input positions receive better attention; a method is therefore needed to select an accuracy-maximizing ordering without explicit query assumptions.

contributions.claim: The paper introduces LLM input reranking: finding an input ranking that maximizes LLM accuracy for a given symmetric-task query without explicit assumptions about the query.
The paper develops efficient algorithms using a helper LLM to estimate input-element relevance and rank-position importance.

author_reported_evidence.claim: The authors report experiments on different synthetic and real datasets.
The authors report that reranking improves LLM accuracy on symmetric tasks by up to 99% proximity to the optimum upper bound.

narrative_sequence.summary: LLMs are practical tools for solving problems across many domains.
The paper studies LLM applications to symmetric tasks over unordered bags of elements, including aggregate queries.
LLMs can overlook elements in large bags because they process ordered inputs, motivating input reranking and algorithms that estimate element relevance and positional importance.
Experiments on synthetic and real datasets are reported to evaluate the proposal and its algorithms.
The authors report accuracy improvements reaching up to 99% proximity to the optimum upper bound.

source_observation.claim: For tasks whose inputs are mathematically unordered, LLM performance can still depend on input order.

interpretation.claim: Input ordering can be treated as a controllable factor for reducing omissions in long-context reasoning.

application.claim: When applying an LLM to unordered collections, evaluate or optimize element ordering before querying the model.

exception.claim: The abstract does not establish whether reranking helps tasks outside symmetric inputs or queries with different assumptions.

source_observation.claim: Optimal reranking depends on both element relevance and the importance of rank positions to LLM attention.

interpretation.claim: Effective input construction may require modeling interactions between content relevance and positional effects.

application.claim: Use a helper model to estimate content and position factors when designing an input-ordering strategy.

exception.claim: The abstract does not specify the helper-LLM assumptions, estimation errors, or computational costs.

unknowns: The abstract does not identify the LLMs, datasets, baselines, metrics, or experimental settings.
The abstract does not explain the reranking algorithms or helper-LLM estimation procedure.
The reported 99% proximity result lacks the underlying task-level values and comparison details.
